mainTopic: Blessings on seeing houses, graves, friends, unusual people and animals, and comets, with teachings about the stars
overview: This amud lists many things we say when we see something. A ברייתא teaches what to say on seeing houses of ישראל or of the nations, whether settled or ruined. In a story, רב חסדא sighs at the ruined house of the generous רב חנא בר חנילאי, and עולא comforts him with teachings of רבי יוחנן. Next come the blessings for seeing graves and for seeing a friend after thirty days or twelve months, followed by a story about three Sages who bless one another. The גמרא then teaches which blessing to say on seeing unusual people. It settles a contradiction about בהקנים: one born that way gets משנה הבריות, and one who became that way later gets דיין האמת. A ברייתא adds blessings for strange animals and for beautiful sights. Finally, the גמרא explains the משנה's זיקין as comets and discusses Orion, Pleiades and other stars, ending with a proof about עש that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What to say on seeing settled or ruined houses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four sayings: for houses of ישראל settled or destroyed, and for houses of the nations settled or destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who sees Jewish houses settled says, 'Blessed… Who sets the border of the widow.' If they are in ruins, he says, 'Blessed is the true Judge.' If he sees houses of the nations settled, he says, 'The house of the proud, ה׳ will uproot.' If they are in ruins, he says, 'God of vengeance, ה׳, God of vengeance, appear!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives four sayings, depending on whose houses you see and what state they are in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sets of houses and two states for each. Settled Jewish homes bring praise that ה׳ protects ישראל, who is compared to a 'widow.' Ruined Jewish homes bring acceptance of ה׳'s judgment, ברוך דיין האמת. For the nations, the sayings are פסוקים rather than full ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Who sets up the border of the widow, a metaphor for ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: There are four cases. Jewish houses settled: מציב גבול אלמנה. Jewish houses ruined: דיין האמת. Houses of the nations settled: בית גאים יסח ה׳. Houses of the nations ruined: אל נקמות.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sees houses of Israel in their settled state,
says: 'Blessed… Who sets the border of the widow.'
In their ruin, he says: 'Blessed is the true Judge.'
Houses of the nations of the world in their settled state,
he says: 'The house of the proud, ה׳ will uproot.'
In their ruin, he says:
'God of vengeance, ה׳, God of vengeance, appear!'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאֶה בָּתֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיִשּׁוּבָן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The saying depends on whose houses you see (ישראל or the nations) and on their state (settled or destroyed).

steps.title: רב חסדא sighs at a ruined house
steps.stepSummary: עולא and רב חסדא are walking. When they reach the doorway of רב חנא בר חנילאי's house, רב חסדא groans and sighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא and רב חסדא were walking on the road. When they reached the doorway of רב חנא בר חנילאי's house, רב חסדא groaned and sighed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a story that ties into the ruined Jewish houses of the ברייתא. This step only sets up the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house is not yet described as ruined; we learn that only later in the story. The sigh is the trigger for everything that comes next.

phrases.english: Ulla and Rav Chisda
were walking on the road.
When they reached the doorway
of the house of Rav Chana bar Chanilai,
Rav Chisda groaned and sighed.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא וְרַב חִסְדָּא הֲווֹ קָא אָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the case of seeing a ruined Jewish house from the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רב חסדא sighs at the house of רב חנא בר חנילאי.

steps.title: עולא asks why he sighs, since sighing harms the body
steps.stepSummary: עולא challenges רב חסדא's sighing. He quotes רב, who says sighing breaks half the body, and רבי יוחנן, who says it breaks the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Why are you sighing? Didn't רב say that sighing breaks half a person's body? As it says, 'And you, son of man, sigh with broken loins.' And רבי יוחנן said it breaks even the whole body. As it says, 'When they ask you why you are sighing, say: because of the news that is coming, and every heart will melt.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא objects to רב חסדא's sigh, because sighing is physically harmful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'why are you sighing?' works as a challenge, not a simple request for information. רב learns from the פסוק that sighing breaks the body down to the loins (half). רבי יוחנן learns from the next פסוק, where the heart melts and every part of the body weakens, that it affects the whole body.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (he) say? Introduces a contradicting source

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ עוּלָּא: אַמַּאי קָא מִתְּנַחַתְּ?
phrases.english: Ulla said to him: Why are you sighing?
But didn't Rav say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָחָה שׁוֹבֶרֶת חֲצִי גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: A sigh breaks half of a person's body,
as it says: 'And you, son of man, sigh'
'with the breaking of the loins, etc.'
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
even a person's entire body,
as it says: 'And when they say to you,'
'Why are you sighing?'
'you shall say: Because of the news that is coming,'
'and every heart will melt, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ עוּלָּא: אַמַּאי קָא מִתְּנַחַתְּ? וְהָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's sigh
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sighing damages half the body (רב) or the whole body (רבי יוחנן), so one should avoid it.

steps.title: רב חסדא describes the house's great kindness
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that this house was famous for its kindness. It had 120 bakers, it fed anyone who came, it guarded the dignity of the poor, and it had doors on all four sides. Now it lies in ruins, so how can he not sigh?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can I not sigh? This was a house with sixty bakers by day and sixty by night, who baked for anyone in need. רב חנא never took his hand out of his purse. He thought: maybe a poor man from a good family will come, and by the time I reach into my purse he will be embarrassed. Also, it had four doors open to the four directions, and whoever came in hungry left full. In years of famine they would throw wheat and barley outside, so that anyone embarrassed to take by day could come and take at night. Now it has fallen into a heap of ruins, and I should not sigh?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends his sigh. The loss of such a kind house is worth the pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every detail shows extra care for the poor and especially for their dignity: the hand already in the purse, the four doors, and the grain left outside at night. The point is that this was not an ordinary house. Its destruction is a real loss for the community.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person from a respectable family

phrases.english: He said to him: How can I not sigh?
A house that had in it
sixty bakers by day
and sixty bakers by night,
and they baked for anyone who needed,
and he never removed his hand from his purse,

phrases.aramaic: דִּסְבַר דִּילְמָא אָתֵי עָנֵי בַּר טוֹבִים
phrases.english: for he thought: perhaps a poor man of good family will come,
and by the time he reaches the purse, he will be embarrassed.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, הֲווֹ פְּתִיחִין לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע בָּבֵי
phrases.english: Moreover, it had four doors open
to the four directions of the world,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל דַּהֲוָה עָיֵיל כָּפֵין נָפֵיק כִּי שָׂבַע.
phrases.english: and whoever entered hungry left satisfied.
And they would throw wheat and barley
outside in years of drought,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל מַאן דִּכְסִיפָא מִילְּתָא לְמִשְׁקַל בִּימָמָא,
phrases.english: so that anyone embarrassed to take by day
could come and take at night.
Now it has fallen into a ruin — and I should not sigh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justification: the size of the loss outweighs the warning against sighing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sighing should be avoided because it harms the body.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruin of so kind a house deserves a sigh.

steps.title: The houses of the righteous were decreed to be destroyed
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן: since the בית המקדש was destroyed, it was decreed that the houses of צדיקים would also be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said. From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, a decree was made on the houses of צדיקים that they would be destroyed. As it says, 'In my ears, ה׳ of hosts: surely many houses will become desolate, great and good ones, without anyone living there.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא begins to comfort רב חסדא. He explains that this ruin is part of a decree, not a random tragedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'great and good' houses, and רבי יוחנן reads that as the homes of צדיקים. Their destruction follows from the חורבן of the מקדש itself. This sets up the comfort in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן —
phrases.english: He said to him: Thus said Rabbi Yochanan:
From the day the Temple was destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: נִגְזְרָה גְּזֵירָה עַל בָּתֵּיהֶן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים שֶׁיֶּחֶרְבוּ,
phrases.english: a decree was issued on the houses of the righteous that they be destroyed,
as it says: 'In my ears, ה׳ of hosts:'

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּתִּים רַבִּים לְשַׁמָּה יִהְיוּ
phrases.english: 'surely many houses will become desolate,'
'great and good, without inhabitant.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא responds to רב חסדא's 'how can I not sigh?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruin is part of a decree that followed the חורבן of the מקדש.

steps.title: ה׳ will restore the houses of the righteous
steps.stepSummary: עולא adds a second teaching of רבי יוחנן. In the future, ה׳ will rebuild the houses of צדיקים, just as He will rebuild הר ציון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will return them to their settled state. As it says, 'A song of ascents of David: Those who trust in ה׳ are like הר ציון.' Just as in the future ה׳ will return הר ציון to its settled state, so too in the future ה׳ will return the houses of צדיקים to their settled state.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the comforting half: the destruction is only temporary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares those who trust in ה׳ to הר ציון. Since הר ציון will be rebuilt, so will the homes of the righteous. The decree from the previous step is not the end of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: To restore them to their settled state
Just as… so too; a comparison formula

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לְיִשּׁוּבָן,
phrases.english: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will restore them to their settled state,
as it says: 'A song of ascents of David:'
'Those who trust in ה׳ are like Mount Zion.'
Just as Mount Zion,

phrases.aramaic: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירוֹ לְיִשּׁוּבוֹ,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, will in the future restore to its settled state,
so too the houses of the righteous,

phrases.aramaic: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לְיִשּׁוּבָן.
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, will in the future restore to their settled state.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לְיִשּׁוּבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comfort with a promise of rebuilding
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruin is temporary, because ה׳ will rebuild the homes of צדיקים together with הר ציון.

steps.title: Enough for a servant to be like his master
steps.stepSummary: עולא sees that רב חסדא is still upset. He tells him it is enough for a servant to be like his Master.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that his mind was still not at ease. He said to him: It is enough for a servant to be like his master.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with עולא's final words of comfort: if ה׳'s own house is in ruins, we can accept the ruin of ours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'Master' is ה׳, and His house is the בית המקדש. Since ה׳ lets His own house lie in ruins, a צדיק's house sharing that fate is fitting. This ties back to the decree that began with the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind was not at ease
It is enough for a servant to be like his master

steps.whatToRemember: Ruined homes of צדיקים reflect the חורבן of ה׳'s own house, the מקדש. They will be rebuilt in the future, and until then a servant should accept sharing his Master's condition.

phrases.english: He saw that his mind was not settled.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דַּיּוֹ לְעֶבֶד שֶׁיְּהֵא כְּרַבּוֹ.
phrases.english: He said to him: It is enough for a servant to be like his master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final comfort after the earlier teachings did not fully settle רב חסדא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since ה׳'s house, the מקדש, lies in ruins, one should accept the ruin of the houses of צדיקים.

steps.title: A blessing upon seeing Jewish graves
steps.stepSummary: A teaching gives the words to say upon seeing קִבְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One who sees Jewish graves says a blessing describing how God formed, fed, sustained, and gathered those buried there in judgment, and will raise them in judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching about what to say upon seeing קִבְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing looks back at the lives of those buried there and forward to their future rising. Each part says that God acts בַּדִּין.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאֶה קִבְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: The Sages taught: One who sees Jewish graves says:
“Blessed … Who formed you in judgment,
and fed you in judgment,
and sustained you in judgment,
and gathered you in judgment,
and will raise you in judgment.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the previous story to a new teaching about blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sees קִבְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל says the stated blessing.

steps.title: An added ending to the blessing
steps.stepSummary: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא gives an ending to the blessing in the name of רַב נַחְמָן.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא concludes it in the name of רב נחמן: God knows the number of you all and will bring you back to life and sustain you. Blessed … Who revives the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a further ending to the blessing over קִבְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first wording ended by saying God will raise those buried there. This ending adds that God knows each of them and closes with a blessing about reviving the dead.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, concludes it,
in the name of Rav Naḥman:
“And Who knows the number of you all,
and He will bring you to life and sustain you.
Blessed … Who revives the dead.”

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ, מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies an additional ending for the blessing just taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessing over קִבְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל can conclude with the stated words about תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים.

steps.title: What is said upon seeing non-Jewish graves
steps.stepSummary: The teaching gives a different response upon seeing קִבְרֵי גוֹיִם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Upon seeing graves of gentiles, one says: “Your mother is ashamed,” and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly gives a separate response for seeing קִבְרֵי גוֹיִם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different case from seeing קִבְרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. The text quotes only the opening words of what is said and marks that the quotation continues.

keyTerms.meaning: and so on; the quotation continues

phrases.english: Upon seeing graves of gentiles, one says:
“Your mother is ashamed,” and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes which graves are being seen and gives a different response.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing קִבְרֵי גוֹיִם calls for the quoted words.

steps.title: Blessings when seeing a friend again
steps.stepSummary: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי gives different blessings after thirty days and after twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: If one sees a friend after thirty days, one says the blessing thanking God for giving us life and bringing us to this time. After twelve months, one says: Blessed … Who revives the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to blessings said when a person sees a friend after a long absence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The length of time changes which blessing is said. Thirty days calls for שֶׁהֶחֱיָינוּ; twelve months calls for מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹאֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: One who sees his friend after thirty days says:
“Blessed … Who has given us life and sustained us
and brought us to this time.”
After twelve months, one says:
“Blessed … Who revives the dead.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הָרוֹאֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from seeing graves to seeing a friend.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After thirty days, one says שֶׁהֶחֱיָינוּ; after twelve months, one says מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים.

steps.title: Why twelve months matters
steps.stepSummary: רַב says that a dead person is forgotten from the heart only after twelve months and cites a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A dead person is not forgotten from the heart until after twelve months, as it says: “I am forgotten from the heart like a dead person; I have become like a lost vessel.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רַב’s teaching and a verse to help explain the twelve-month point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The preceding rule used twelve months for מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים. רַב connects that length of time with how a dead person fades from the heart; the verse supplies his wording.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A dead person is not forgotten from the heart
until after twelve months.
As it is stated:
“I am forgotten from the heart like a dead person;
I have become like a lost vessel.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֵין הַמֵּת מִשְׁתַּכֵּחַ מִן הַלֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the significance of the twelve-month period just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The significance of twelve months in the blessing for seeing a friend again.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רַב’s teaching, supported by the quoted verse.

steps.title: Three Sages meet on the road
steps.stepSummary: Two Sages traveling together encounter רַב חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע were walking on the road. They met רב חנינא בריה דרב איקא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a story about a meeting. This prepares for the blessings the Sages say when they see one another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one has made an argument yet. The meeting gives a real-life setting for the blessings just discussed.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,
were walking on the road.

phrases.aramaic: פְּגַעוּ בֵּיהּ בְּרַב חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא.
phrases.english: They met Rav Ḥanina, son of Rav Ika.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that puts blessings upon meeting people into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This narrative line sets up the encounter; it does not state a new ruling.

steps.title: They say two blessings upon seeing him
steps.stepSummary: The two travelers tell רַב חֲנִינָא that they said blessings for his wisdom and for seeing him again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: When we saw you, we recited two blessings over you: “Blessed … Who has shared of His wisdom with those who revere Him,” and “Who has given us life.”
steps.whatsHappening: The two Sages tell רַב חֲנִינָא which two blessings they said upon seeing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One blessing responds to his wisdom. The other is שֶׁהֶחֱיָינוּ, the blessing for seeing someone again after an absence.

keyTerms.meaning: Who has shared of His wisdom with those who revere Him

phrases.english: They said to him: When we saw you,
we recited two blessings over you:
“Blessed … Who has shared of His wisdom with those who revere Him”
and “Who has given us life.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: בַּהֲדֵי דַּחֲזֵינָךְ בָּרֵיכִינַן עֲלָךְ תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports what the travelers said when the meeting occurred.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The travelers report saying a blessing for wisdom and שֶׁהֶחֱיָינוּ.

steps.title: He says he recited a third blessing
steps.stepSummary: רַב חֲנִינָא says he regarded the two travelers as equivalent to six hundred thousand Jews and added חֲכַם הָרָזִים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: When I saw you, I considered you like six hundred thousand of the house of Israel. I recited three blessings over you: those same two and “Blessed … Who knows the secrets.”
steps.whatsHappening: רַב חֲנִינָא answers that he said the same two blessings and one more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says he regarded the two men as equivalent to a gathering of six hundred thousand Jews. On that basis, he added חֲכַם הָרָזִים; the text reports his reasoning as part of the story.

phrases.english: He said to them: I too,
when I saw you, considered you in my eyes
like six hundred thousand of the house of Israel,
and I recited three blessings over you:
those same two,
and “Blessed … Who knows the secrets.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזִתִינְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the travelers’ account with a surprising third blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רַב חֲנִינָא reports adding חֲכַם הָרָזִים because of how he regarded the two travelers.

steps.title: The meeting ends suddenly
steps.stepSummary: The travelers react to רַב חֲנִינָא’s remark; the story ends with his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Are you that clever? They fixed their eyes upon him, and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story by reporting the travelers’ reaction and what happened next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their words respond to his surprising claim about the third blessing. The text then reports that they fixed their gaze on him and he died; it gives no further discussion of the blessings here.

keyTerms.meaning: they fixed their eyes upon him

phrases.english: They said to him: Are you that clever!
They fixed their eyes upon him, and he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the account of the three blessings.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story ends with רַב חֲנִינָא’s death, without further argument about his third blessing.

steps.title: A blessing upon seeing spotted skin
steps.stepSummary: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי assigns מְשַׁנֶּה הַבְּרִיּוֹת to seeing people with spotted skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: One who sees people with spotted skin says: “Blessed … Who makes creatures different.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about the blessing said upon seeing people with spotted skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is הַבַּהֲקָנִים. This ruling matters immediately because the next source assigns that same case a different blessing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who sees people with spotted skin says:
“Blessed … Who makes creatures different.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הָרוֹאֶה אֶת הַבַּהֲקָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and begins a new rule about blessings upon seeing people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Upon seeing הַבַּהֲקָנִים, one says מְשַׁנֶּה הַבְּרִיּוֹת.

steps.title: A source gives spotted skin a different blessing
steps.stepSummary: A challenge quotes two lists of physical conditions. It places הַבַּהֲקָנִים in the list whose blessing is דַּיֵּין אֱמֶת.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection is raised: For the first group of unusual physical features, one says “Who makes creatures different.” For the second group—including people with spotted skin—one says “the true Judge.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling about הַבַּהֲקָנִים by quoting a source that gives them a different blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read both lists carefully: the first gets מְשַׁנֶּה אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת, while the second gets דַּיֵּין אֱמֶת. הַבַּהֲקָנִים appear in the second list, directly conflicting with the previous ruling. This passage stops before an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: a person with unusually white skin

phrases.english: An objection is raised: If one saw a person with unusually dark skin,
a person with unusually red skin, or a person with unusually white skin,
an unusually tall person, or a dwarf,
or a person with warts, one says:
“Blessed … Who makes creatures different.”
For a person missing a limb or a blind person,
a person with a flat head or a lame person,
a person afflicted with boils or people with spotted skin,
one says: “Blessed … the true Judge”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes a conflicting ruling for the very condition named in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי’s ruling that הַבַּהֲקָנִים receive מְשַׁנֶּה הַבְּרִיּוֹת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The quoted source explicitly includes הַבַּהֲקָנִים among those for whom one says דַּיֵּין אֱמֶת instead.

steps.title: Born spotted versus became spotted later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: משנה הבריות is for someone spotted from birth, and דיין האמת is for someone who became spotted after birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, where we say משנה הבריות, is about someone spotted from his mother's womb. That one, where we say דיין האמת, is about someone who became spotted after he was born.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 18. It explains that the two sources are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said to bless משנה הבריות on a בהקן, but the ברייתא listed בהקנים under דיין האמת. The answer splits the case by timing. A person born this way shows the variety of creation, so we say משנה הבריות. A person who became this way later suffered a misfortune, so we say דיין האמת, the blessing on bad news.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources fit together
From his mother's womb, meaning from birth
The True Judge; the blessing said on bad tidings

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is from his mother's womb,
phrases.notes: This is the case where רבי יהושע בן לוי says to bless 'משנה הבריות'.

phrases.english: that one is after he was born.
phrases.notes: This is the case where the ברייתא says to bless 'דיין האמת'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא מִמְּעֵי אִמּוֹ, הָא בָּתַר דְּאִיתְיְלִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to discuss the same spotted person, so they seemed to give conflicting blessings.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blessing depends on when the condition began: from birth it is משנה הבריות, after birth it is דיין האמת.

steps.title: The wording of the ברייתא supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the spotted person next to an amputee, whose condition usually comes after birth. This supports the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, because the ברייתא teaches the spotted person alongside an amputee. Conclude from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא's own wording backs up the answer it just gave, and then it closes the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An amputee (קיטע) usually loses a limb through an accident or illness after birth. Since the ברייתא groups the בהקן with the amputee, its בהקן must also be a case of something that happened later. That fits דיין האמת, and the answer is confirmed with שמע מינה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise; the wording supports this
Amputee, a person missing a limb
Conclude from it; the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: For a person with an unusual condition, the blessing depends on timing. From birth you say משנה הבריות. If it happened later, you say דיין האמת.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
for it teaches it alongside an amputee.
phrases.notes: An amputee's condition usually comes after birth.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer from step 19 with a precise reading of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתא's בהקן became spotted after birth
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists the בהקן next to the קיטע (amputee)
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The answer is confirmed: the ברייתא's דיין האמת applies to someone whose condition began after birth.

steps.title: Blessings on strange animals and on beautiful creatures and trees
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches two blessings. For an elephant, monkey, or קיפוף you say משנה הבריות. For beautiful creatures or trees you say שככה לו בעולמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who sees an elephant, a monkey, or a קיפוף says, "Blessed… Who makes creatures different." One who sees beautiful creatures or beautiful trees says, "Blessed… Who has such things in His world."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two more blessings about things we see: one for odd-looking animals and one for beautiful sights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Odd-looking animals show how varied God made creation, so we say משנה הבריות. Especially beautiful people, animals, or trees show the beauty of God's world, so we say שככה לו בעולמו.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual-looking bird (a vulture according to רש"י; others say an owl)
Who has such things in His world; the blessing on beautiful sights

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sees an elephant, a monkey, or a vulture,
says: "Blessed… Who makes creatures different."
If he saw beautiful creatures or beautiful trees,
he says: "Blessed… Who has such things in His world."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאָה פִּיל, קוֹף וְקִפֹוף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from people with unusual conditions to more blessings on unusual and beautiful sights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strange animals get משנה הבריות. Beautiful creatures and trees get שככה לו בעולמו.

steps.title: What are זיקין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's word זיקין and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding the זיקין in the משנה: what are זיקין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a word in the משנה and asks for its definition. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that on זיקין you bless שכחו וגבורתו מלא עולם. Before we can apply that blessing, we have to know what a זיק actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: A sky phenomenon from the משנה that gets the blessing שכחו וגבורתו מלא עולם

phrases.english: Regarding the zikin:
What are zikin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to define a new term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word זיקין

steps.title: שמואל defines זיקין as a comet
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says זיקין are a כוכבא דשביט, a comet.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is a comet, literally a 'star with a rod' or tail.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question: זיקין are comets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comet looks like a star with a long tail, like a rod (שביט) stretched across the sky. That is the sight that gets the blessing שכחו וגבורתו מלא עולם.

keyTerms.meaning: A comet; literally a star with a rod or tail

phrases.english: Shmuel said: A comet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.

steps.title: שמואל knows the sky except for comets
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says he knows the paths of the sky as well as the streets of his city נהרדעא, except for comets.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The paths of the sky are as clear to me as the paths of נהרדעא, except for the comet, which I do not know what it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another statement of שמואל about comets: even he, an expert in astronomy, did not understand them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was a great expert in astronomy. His admission that comets were a mystery shows how unusual they are. This also explains why seeing one calls for a blessing on God's power.

keyTerms.meaning: Are clear or familiar to me

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The paths of the sky are clear to me
like the paths of Neharde'a,
except for the comet,
which I do not know what it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: נְהִירִין לִי שְׁבִילֵי דִשְׁמַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related statement from the same speaker about comets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comets were beyond even שמואל's expert understanding of the sky.

steps.title: A tradition that a comet never crosses Orion
steps.stepSummary: There is a tradition that a comet does not pass through כסלא (Orion), and if it did, the world would be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we have a tradition that a comet does not cross Orion. If it did cross Orion, the world would be destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a received tradition about comets. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גמירי means this is a passed-down tradition, not a logical argument. It claims that a comet crossing Orion would be catastrophic for the world.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (a received teaching)

phrases.english: And we have a tradition that it does not cross Orion,
and if it crosses Orion, the world would be destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of comets with a tradition about them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A comet never crosses Orion; if it did, the world would be destroyed.

steps.title: But we see comets crossing Orion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the tradition: we can see comets crossing Orion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we do see that it crosses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the tradition from step 25 using what people actually see in the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If comets never cross Orion, how can people see one doing so while the world still exists? Observation seems to contradict the tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: But we do see; a challenge from observation

phrases.english: But we see that it does cross!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the tradition in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The tradition that a comet never crosses Orion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Observation shows comets crossing Orion, yet the world has not been destroyed.

steps.title: Only the comet's glow crosses
steps.stepSummary: Only the comet's glow (זיו) crosses Orion, and that makes it look as if the comet itself crossed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is its glow that crosses, and it only looks as though the comet itself crossed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. What we see crossing is the comet's light, not the comet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition still holds, because the body of the comet never actually crosses. Its long tail of light reaches past Orion and fools the eye.

phrases.english: It is its glow that crosses,
and it appears as though it itself crossed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comet itself seemed to cross Orion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only its glow crosses, so the tradition stands.

steps.title: רב הונא: a sky-curtain tears open
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the sight is really the וילון (a layer of sky) tearing and rolling back, revealing the light of the next רקיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: It is the וילון that tears and rolls up, showing the light of the next firmament.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the challenge: what looks like a comet crossing Orion is not a comet at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא explains the sight as a gap opening in the וילון, the lowest heavenly layer. Light from the רקיע behind it shines through and looks like a moving comet. Since nothing actually crosses Orion, the tradition is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Curtain; the name of the lowest heavenly layer

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is the vilon that tears,
which rolls up and shows the light of the firmament.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: וִילוֹן הוּא דְּמִקְּרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same challenge as step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A comet was seen crossing Orion.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the וילון tearing open and showing light, not a comet crossing.

steps.title: רב אשי: a startled star on the other side
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a star moves away on one side of Orion, and a star on the other side sees it, gets startled, and shudders. This makes it look as if something crossed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is a star that moves away from one side of Orion. Its fellow star on the other side sees it, is startled, and looks as if it crossed.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: two separate stars, one on each side of Orion, create the illusion of a crossing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing actually passes through Orion. One star shifts on one side and another star shudders on the other side, so it looks like one object traveled across. The tradition remains true.

keyTerms.meaning: Was uprooted, moved from its place

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹכְבָא הוּא דְּעָקַר מֵהַאי גִּיסָא דְכִסְלָא
phrases.english: It is a star that is uprooted from this side of Orion,
and its fellow on the other side sees it,
and is startled, and appears like one that crossed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כּוֹכְבָא הוּא דְּעָקַר מֵהַאי גִּיסָא דְכִסְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two stars on opposite sides create the appearance of a crossing.
steps.whatToRemember: All three answers keep the tradition that nothing really crosses Orion. They differ only in what the misleading sight actually is: the comet's glow, a torn sky-curtain, or a startled star.

steps.title: Two פסוקים list Orion and Pleiades in opposite orders
steps.stepSummary: שמואל points out that one פסוק (איוב) puts כסיל before כימה, and another (עמוס) puts כימה before כסיל. He asks how to reconcile them.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל raised a contradiction. It is written, "Who makes Ursa Major, Orion, and Pleiades," and it is written, "Who makes Pleiades and Orion." How can this be?
steps.whatsHappening: Staying with stars, the גמרא brings שמואל's question about two פסוקים that list the same two constellations in reverse order. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק mentions כסיל (Orion) first, and the other mentions כימה (Pleiades) first. A change of order suggests that neither one is simply more important than the other, and שמואל asks what that teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? How do we reconcile it?

phrases.english: Shmuel raised a contradiction.
It is written: "Who makes Ursa Major, Orion, and Pleiades"
and it is written: "Who makes Pleiades and Orion."
How is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל רָמֵי. כְּתִיב ״עֹשֶׂה עָשׁ כְּסִיל וְכִימָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from Orion and comets to a related contradiction about Orion in the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the constellations in איוב and עמוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two פסוקים reverse the order of כסיל and כימה, so which one comes first?

steps.title: Orion's heat and Pleiades' cold balance each other
steps.stepSummary: The order switches because each constellation is needed to balance the other: כסיל's heat offsets כימה's cold, and כימה's cold offsets כסיל's heat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Were it not for the heat of Orion, the world could not survive the cold of Pleiades. And were it not for the cold of Pleiades, the world could not survive the heat of Orion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers שמואל's contradiction. Each constellation is equally necessary, so each one gets to be listed first in one פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither constellation is more important. Each one protects the world from the extreme of the other. Listing each one first in one פסוק shows that they are equal partners in keeping the world in balance.
steps.whatToRemember: The reversed order in the פסוקים teaches that Orion's heat and Pleiades' cold are equally needed. Each one keeps the world from the other's extreme.

phrases.english: Were it not for the heat of Orion,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִתְקַיֵּים עוֹלָם מִפְּנֵי צִינָּה שֶׁל כִּימָה,
phrases.english: the world could not exist because of the cold of Pleiades,
and were it not for the cold of Pleiades,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִתְקַיֵּים עוֹלָם מִפְּנֵי חַמָּה שֶׁל כְּסִיל.
phrases.english: the world could not exist because of the heat of Orion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's contradiction from step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both orders are correct because the two are mutually dependent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One constellation should come first because it is more important.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are equally needed, so each comes first in one פסוק.

steps.title: The scorpion constellation's tail rests in the river of fire
steps.stepSummary: There is a tradition that the tail of the scorpion constellation (עקרב) lies in the נהר דינור. Without this, nobody stung by a scorpion would survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition: if the tail of the scorpion constellation were not resting in the river of fire, anyone stung by a scorpion would not live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a tradition that fits the theme of the last steps. Strong star forces are held in check so the world can survive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 showed that כסיל and כימה balance each other's heat and cold. Here is one more example of a dangerous star force being held back. The power of the scorpion constellation is weakened because its tail sits in the נהר דינור, and that is why scorpion stings are not always deadly.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (passed down, not derived from a verse)

phrases.english: And we have a tradition: if not for
the tail of the Scorpion constellation
which rests in the river of fire,
anyone whom
a scorpion stung
would not live.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example of heavenly forces being held in balance, after the כסיל and כימה balance in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scorpion constellation's tail rests in the נהר דינור, which weakens its power. Otherwise every scorpion sting would kill.

steps.title: A verse in איוב shows God controls these star forces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea with God's words to איוב about binding כימה and loosening כסיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what God said to איוב: "Can you tie the bonds of כימה, or loosen the cords of כסיל?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to back up the idea that God holds back and releases the powers of the stars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God asks איוב whether he can tie up כימה or untie כסיל. The point is that only God balances these forces, holding one back and releasing the other so the world can survive. This matches the heat-and-cold balance described in step 31.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what (the verse means)

phrases.english: And this is what was said to him
by the Merciful One, to Job:
"Can you bind the chains of Kimah (Pleiades)
or loosen the cords of Kesil (Orion)?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a verse supporting the theme of God balancing the star forces.
steps.raayaObject: That God holds back and releases the powers of the constellations to keep the world in balance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 38:31, where God asks whether איוב can bind כימה or loosen כסיל.
steps.whatToRemember: The stars have powerful effects (heat, cold, danger), and God keeps them balanced so the world can survive.

steps.title: What does the name כימה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כימה is and why it has that name.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is "כימה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what the word כימה, which just appeared in the פסוק, means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having used כימה in the verse, the גמרא wants to explain the name itself. This is a request for a definition, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A constellation, usually identified as the Pleiades

phrases.english: What is "Kimah"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the verse to defining one of its words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning or origin of the name כימה.

steps.title: שמואל says כימה is about a hundred stars
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that כימה sounds like כמאה, meaning about a hundred stars. There is a further dispute over whether those stars are bunched together or spread out.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: it means "about a hundred" stars. Some say they are gathered together, and some say they are scattered.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that the name כימה is a play on the words כמאה, about a hundred. Then two opinions are given on how those stars are arranged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name is explained by its sound: כימה sounds like כ־מאה, about one hundred. The two views that follow do not argue with שמואל. They only disagree about whether the hundred stars sit close together or are spread apart.
steps.confusionAlert: The two אמרי לה views are not arguing with שמואל about the number. Both accept about a hundred stars and differ only on how they are arranged.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
about a hundred stars.
Some say they are gathered together,
and some say they are scattered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כימה is named for being about a hundred (כמאה) stars. Whether they are clustered or spread out is disputed.

steps.title: What is the star called עש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what עש, a star group named in איוב, is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is "עש"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another star name, עש. It comes from a פסוק in איוב ("עושה עש כסיל וכימה"). This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps defining the star names from the איוב verses. This is another request for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: A star group named in איוב, often translated Ursa Major

phrases.english: What is "Ash"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining star names, now moving from כימה to עש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the star group called עש.

steps.title: רב יהודה identifies עש as יותא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that עש is the star group called יותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: it is יותא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers by giving the name people used in his day for עש, which is יותא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה swaps the biblical name for the common Aramaic one. That name was unclear too, so it leads straight to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Aramaic name for the star group עש

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Yota.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עש is the star group known as יותא.

steps.title: What is יותא?
steps.stepSummary: Because the name יותא is also unclear, the גמרא asks what it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is "יותא"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of רב יהודה's answer, since יותא is also an unfamiliar word. This sets up two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer can raise a new question when it uses a term that is not clear. Here the גמרא digs one level deeper to pin down which stars are meant.

phrases.english: What is "Yota"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to clarify the term used in step 37's answer.

steps.title: Two views: the tail of Aries or the head of Taurus
steps.stepSummary: One view says יותא is the tail of טלה (Aries). Another says it is the head of עגלא (Taurus).
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it is the tail of the Ram (Aries), and some say it is the head of the Calf (Taurus).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different opinions about which group of stars יותא is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views place יותא at the border area between two neighboring zodiac signs. One puts it at the end of טלה, and the other puts it at the start of the next sign, שור/עגלא. The next step decides between them.

phrases.english: Some say: the tail of the Ram (Aries).
And some say: the head of the Calf (Taurus).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 38 with two competing identifications.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יותא is either the tail of טלה or the head of עגלא.

steps.title: A verse supports the view that יותא is the tail of Aries
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא favors the view that יותא is the tail of טלה. It cites "ועיש על בניה תנחם," which shows that עיש is missing something. A tail would look cut short in this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to follow the one who says it is the tail of the Ram, as it is written: "And can you comfort עיש over her children?" This shows she is missing something, and she appears...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides between the two views using a פסוק. It argues that עיש is described as lacking something, which fits a tail. The sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks of comforting עיש over her children, so עיש must have lost something and be incomplete. A tail looks like something cut off or trailing behind, which fits this picture better than a head does. So the verse supports the view that יותא is זנב טלה.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical / it makes sense

steps.confusionAlert: This passage stops in the middle of a sentence after the word ומתחזיא ("and she appears"). The description of how she appears continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: And it is logical like the one who says
the tail of the Ram, as it is written:
"And Ayish, can you comfort her over her children?"
Evidently, she is lacking, and she appears
phrases.notes: Sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views of step 39 using a verse.
steps.raayaObject: That יותא (עש) is the tail of טלה, not the head of עגלא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 38:32, "ועיש על בניה תנחם," which describes עיש as lacking something, as a tail would appear.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא explains star names from איוב: כימה means about a hundred stars, and עש is יותא, best identified as the tail of טלה because the verse describes it as missing something.
